title: Dispatch: item economy reset/timer executor (attempt 1)
description:
Implement the deterministic item economy reset/timer executor specified by parent bead eshyra-c7sx (read `bd show eshyra-c7sx` first for scope, rationale, and acceptance criteria). This plan pins the design decisions; follow it unless the code contradicts it, in which case record the contradiction in your completion notes.

## Code survey (verified 2026-07-20, commit 958d6d0)

- `packages/core/src/state/rest.ts:159` `advanceWorldTime` is the ONLY clock-advance path; it already runs `expireElapsedWorldEffects` and `resolveStableRecoveries` inside its transaction and returns their evidence on `WorldClock`. Rest completion (`complete()`, rest.ts:485) calls it inside the same txn, then applies per-event restores (`restoreSpellSlots`, `resetUsage` with event `short_rest`/`long_rest`) per participant.
- `AdvanceWorldTimeInput` (rest.ts:32) has NO rng today. Tools have `ctx.rng` (see `spendRestHitDieTool`).
- `packages/core/src/state/itemState.ts`: `ItemEconomyState` = `{remaining, availableAt?, lastReset?}` (strings for the latter two; validated at itemState.ts:220-246 but NEVER written anywhere today). `useItem` (itemState.ts:1463) spends economies, resolves depletion (`resolveItemDepletion`), schedules `pendingTimers` via `resolveItemStateTimers`, and writes state through `validateItemStateForRecord` + `writeItemState`. `readItemState`/`writeItemState` are the authoritative row access.
- `packages/core/src/state/itemTimers.ts`: `resolveItemStateTimers` anchors at the CURRENT clock; timer deadlines are absolute `deadlineElapsedMinutes`. Round-unit timers are rejected (encounter-round scheduler is out of scope here too).
- `packages/core/src/state/itemDepletion.ts`: depletion rolls (destroyedOn/regainOn/loseProperty/becomes) happen at spend time. `lifecycle.pendingTerminal === 'destroyed'` is written by useItem (deferred destruction while a machine lifecycle is still active, e.g. bead-of-force sphere) and today NOTHING ever completes it.
- Committed pack (rules__dnd5e-srd-5.1): 240 magic items, 81 with economy resets, exactly 11 distinct reset shapes (enumerate them yourself from records.json to build the test matrix; the list below is verified):
  1. charges/dawn/dice-expr (39; e.g. cube-of-force, gem-of-seeing)
  2. charges/dawn/all (eyes-of-charming)
  3. charges/dusk/dice-expr (robe-of-stars)
  4. charges/days:7/all (figurine-of-wondrous-power; onDepleted becomes inert)
  5. per-day/dawn/all (31)
  6. per-day/long-rest/all (ring-of-x-ray-vision)
  7. cooldown/hour/all (frost-brand etc.; cooldown.duration 1 hour)
  8. cooldown/days:7/all (horn-of-valhalla, rod-of-security; cooldown.duration 7 day)
  9. budget/days/all (manuals/tomes, days:36500 = SRD century; onDepleted loseProperty+inert)
  10. budget/long-rest/all (boots-of-speed)
  11. budget/per-period/DurationSpec amount, period 12h, onlyIfUnused (winged-boots)
- Timer transitions (12, all via-less, minute/hour units, two dice-amount: potion-of-diminution/growth 1d4 hour). One pack defect: cube-of-force declares `stateMachine.duration` {1,minute} with NO timer transition and prose-only termination — its expiry is unexecutable as declared. Do NOT work around it; fail closed (schedule/execute nothing for duration-without-timer-transition) and file an importer finding with `bd create` (label: importer) describing it.

## Design decisions (binding)

1. **Module**: new `packages/core/src/state/itemResetExecutor.ts` exporting (internal surface only — export via `internal.ts`, NOT the root index):
   - `resolveDueItemClockEvents(txn, {campaignId, previousElapsedMinutes, elapsedMinutes, rng?, provenance, sessionId, at})` — clock-derived resets + pendingTimers, called from `advanceWorldTime` after `resolveStableRecoveries`, campaign-wide (all item_state rows, including items not currently held by a character).
   - `resolveRestEventItemResets(txn, {campaignId, event: 'short-rest'|'long-rest', participants, rng?, ...ctx})` — called from `complete()` in the per-participant phase, scoped to inventory held by rest participants.
   Both return evidence arrays; surface them on `WorldClock` (new field `itemResets`, `itemTimerResolutions`) and in rest `benefits` (persisted in benefits_json).
2. **Dawn/dusk are clock-derived, not a DM tool call.** Convention (document it): `elapsed_minutes ≡ 0` is midnight; minute-of-day = `elapsed_minutes mod 1440`; dawn = minute 360 (06:00), dusk = minute 1080 (18:00). A boundary fires for each crossing in the half-open interval `(previousElapsedMinutes, elapsedMinutes]`; advancing 3 days fires 3 dawns (dice regains roll per crossing, clamped at max — 'all' resets are naturally idempotent). Rationale to record in the doc: deterministic and testable, no new tool surface, the DM already owns elapsed minutes via advance_time, and free-text narration labels are already tracked via narrativeLabelStale. Write the semantics doc at `docs/item-reset-executor.md` (anchoring, per-period anchor, onlyIfUnused definition, fail-closed rules, idempotence keys) and link it from the restore_usage tool description's "semantic reset owner" phrase if a short pointer fits.
3. **RNG threading**: add optional `rng?: Rng` to `AdvanceWorldTimeInput` and `CompleteRestInput`; pass `ctx.rng` from `advanceTimeTool` and the rest tools. Fail closed: if a due reset/timer needs dice and rng is undefined, throw (aborting the txn) with a message naming the pack ref and shape.
4. **Idempotence**: per-economy `lastReset` = decimal string of the elapsed minute of the last applied boundary. A boundary applies iff `boundary > Number(lastReset ?? -1)` AND `boundary` lies in `(prev, next]`. The half-open interval already prevents re-firing across calls; lastReset is the recorded evidence + guard for any secondary path.
5. **hour/days anchors** (`availableAt`): these resets are anchored at a use event, not the calendar. Extend `useItem` cost application: when a spend brings an economy's `remaining` to 0 and the economy declares an `hour`/`days` reset (equivalently kind cooldown with cooldown.duration — verify the declared reset entry and cooldown.duration agree; mismatch = importer finding), set `availableAt` = String(spendElapsed + durationMinutes) where duration = cooldown.duration if present else days*1440 / 60 for hour. Executor: when `elapsedMinutes >= Number(availableAt)`, restore per the reset amount ('all' → max), clear `availableAt`, set `lastReset`. Pre-existing state rows without `availableAt` simply never come due — document this as the migration posture (no DB migration needed; state lives in item_state JSON).
6. **per-period + onlyIfUnused** (winged-boots): ANY spend of the economy overwrites `availableAt` = String(spendElapsed + periodMinutes) (this IS the onlyIfUnused definition: the period restarts on use — document it). Executor: while `Number(availableAt) <= elapsedMinutes` and `remaining < max`: `remaining = min(max, remaining + amountInBudgetUnits)`, `availableAt += periodMinutes`, set lastReset. Convert the DurationSpec amount into the SAME units `remaining` uses for budget economies — read `initialRemaining`/`durationRoundTicks` (itemState.ts:646-778) and reuse/extract that conversion; do not invent a second one.
7. **Regain clamp / 'all' target**: max must come from the same source `createInitialItemState` used — declared numeric max, or the seeded `randomInitialization` result for dice-derived maxima. Extract or reuse a `resolveEconomyMax(state, economy)` helper from the existing init logic. If the max is unrecoverable, fail closed (throw naming the instance + economy).
8. **Lifecycle gating**: `nonmagical` and `consumed` (and pendingTerminal) items never regain. `inert` regains ONLY when the resetting economy has a recorded depletion whose `becomes === 'inert'` (see `state.depletions`); applying that reset restores the economy AND removes the inert lifecycle (figurine after 7 days, manuals after a century). All state writes go through `validateItemStateForRecord` + `writeItemState`.
9. **pendingTimers execution**: resolve timers with `deadlineElapsedMinutes <= elapsedMinutes`, oldest first, per item: set `machineState = to`, drop the fired timer, then schedule the entered state's own timer transitions ANCHORED AT THE FIRED DEADLINE (not at `now`) so chains (eversmoking-bottle cloud-60 → cloud-growing → …) stay accurate across a large advance; cascade until no timer is due. `resolveItemStateTimers` anchors at the current clock — add an explicit anchor parameter rather than duplicating it. Surface fired transitions' `effects` in the evidence. If a fired transition lands on `destroyed` (bead-of-force sphere→destroyed) or the machine resolves while `lifecycle.pendingTerminal === 'destroyed'`, complete destruction via the same path useItem uses (`destroyInventoryItem`), surfacing attunementsEnded.
10. **Fail closed on unknown shapes**: any reset entry not matching the 11 shapes above (or a schema-legal combination this executor does not implement, e.g. numeric amount with at:'dawn') throws with pack ref + JSON of the entry. Never skip silently, never approximate.
11. **No new tables/migrations**: all state stays in item_state JSON; evidence rides tool results and rest benefits_json.

## Acceptance criteria (from the parent bead; all must have tests)

Every one of the 11 pack reset shapes exercised end-to-end (dawn dice regain with clamp; dawn all; dusk; per-day all at dawn; per-day long-rest; budget long-rest; budget per-period with onlyIfUnused including "use resets the period"; days cooldown incl. figurine inert-clear and manual century; hour cooldown); timers fire deterministically on advance_time AND on rest completion with recorded evidence (including a cascade case and a destruction case with attunement evidence); double-application impossible (advance twice / advance-then-rest across the same boundary; crossing 3 dawns rolls 3 times); fail closed on missing rng and on unknown shapes; inert/nonmagical/consumed non-regain cases; cube-of-force duration finding filed as a bead, not executed. Follow existing test conventions (see packages/core/test/itemState.test.ts, rest.test.ts / restRecovery tests) in a new `packages/core/test/itemResetExecutor.test.ts` plus targeted additions where wiring lives.

## Environment / workflow caveats

- Work ONLY in this worktree; run `cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"` first; `npm ci` before building.
- `npm run verify:worktree` must be fully green before commit (Biome warnings fail CI).
- This touches magic-item mechanics consumers but NOT the importer/pack data: do not edit anything under packages/core/data/rules-packs or packages/core/scripts/importers. Pack defects are beads, not edits.
- New exports go through `packages/core/src/internal.ts` only.
- Commit on this branch; do not push; do not open a PR (integration is handled after review).
